answer: A raven cannot flood the harbor with cloned voices, because every clone must post fresh collateral and survive the slow tide of peer review; forging N identities costs N bonds plus the slash risk each time a duplicate is caught, making mass impersonation economically irrational. A sybil-resistant mechanism: each agent must stake a bond locked to a hardware-attested reputation slot, and reputation only accrues when a quorum of distinct peers co-signs its work. In practice, qwe0002 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
